Visit OIC Brighton, Your Way
OXFORD INTERNATIONAL COLLEGE (OIC) BRIGHTON
INSPIRING EXCELLENCE
Pre-GCSE Ages 13-14
GCSE Ages 14-16
A-Level 16-18
SET FOR SUCCESS
A WORLD OF OPPORTUNITY
The leading independent college in Brighton, our unique approach prepares students for success at universities and in careers around the globe.
Our culture of excellence inspires our students to go above and beyond to be their very best. Here, you’ll follow your own pathway to success – based entirely around your talents, interests, and goals –which will inspire you to excel academically and fulfil your university and career ambitions.
Whatever your goals – whether it’s a dream university course or along-term career plan – our pioneering approach to education will get you exactly where you want to go.
From the moment you join us, we’ll work together to map out a bespoke learning journey, designed around your strengths and interests. Your tailored Global Strategic Pathway will feature three pillars: academic excellence, personal growth, and career preparation. This approach is designed for high achievers who aspire to the most competitive courses at the best universities in the world.
Our academic pillar includes the GCSE or A-level subjects you choose. Whichever route you take, you’ll benefit from expert teaching and unwavering guidance. You’ll learn alongside like-minded students in dynamic classes where ideas, creativity, and individuality flourish. You’ll also receive dedicated one-to-one mentoring from your very own Strategy Tutor.
Innovators, progressive thinkers, and trailblazers: OIC Brighton teachers are at the forefront of educational best practice. Recruited from prestigious UK and international schools, they bring a wealth of experience and expertise to our cutting-edge classrooms and learning spaces.
Our teachers know what it takes to inspire excellence. Leaders in their field, they embrace innovation, deliver extraordinary learning experiences, and nurture individual strengths and talents. Many have excelled in the industry they teach in, too.
Every single one of our educators is handpicked, based not only on their impressive qualifications and extensive UK and international experience, but also their commitment to our vision. Through a rigorous recruitment process, we make sure their values align with our high expectations and ambitious culture.
Our teachers cultivate a collaborative environment where you can confidently express yourself and share your ideas. Their enthusiasm and pioneering spirit ensure every lesson and experience is energising and engaging, too – and that you’re always inspired to go above and beyond.
Outside the classroom, our team work tirelessly to bring out the best in each student. Strong partnerships enrich every aspect of our learners’ experience, whether that’s through shared passions, during mealtimes, or through our Supercurricular activities. You’ll also be allocated a dedicated Strategy Tutor, who will mentor you throughout your time with us. Their holistic support includes regular catch-up meetings and one-to-one pastoral care.
History and modernity seamlessly combine on our spectacular single-site campus. Set among 23 acres of parks and ancient woodland – and located just minutes away from the coast and city – our beautiful countryside setting is the perfect place to live and learn.
Our stunning campus is unlike any other. We’ve invested more than £35 million to create an awe-inspiring setting that effortlessly blends impressive 18th century architecture with state-of-the-art learning spaces and facilities. The result? A quintessentially English college environment that’s purpose-built to meet the ambitions of our 21st century learners.
Set among 23 acres of verdant parkland, woods, and rolling hills, our campus is perfectly positioned, too. Beautiful outdoor areas are ideal for studying, fitness, and spending time with friends. They also offer endless opportunities to simply connect with nature and boost wellbeing. Excitingly, the college is just minutes from the beaches and bright lights of buzzing Brighton. We’re also close to the South Downs, a designated area of natural beauty, and easily accessible from London.
On campus, like-minded students motivate and support one another to achieve their goals in bright classrooms, collaborative study areas, and quiet learning spaces. Innovation flourishes in our six ultra-modern science labs, which are enhanced by top-of-the-range education technology, and finished to the highest specifications. And in our many shared spaces – which include a contemporary café, sixth form centre, gym, prayer room, Learning Resource Centre, and dining room – our closeknit community comes together to learn, have fun, and create lasting memories.
Wherever you are on our campus, there’s always a book within reach. Our decentralised library gives students the opportunity to immerse themselves in world-class works of fact and fiction, as they indulge their passion for reading.
Your journey to success at OIC Brighton will extend beyond academics. Our pioneering approach will nurture your personal growth and career aspirations, ensuring you have the skills, experiences, and extra qualifications you need to thrive at your dream university.
At OIC Brighton, we understand that academic success is just one element of what’s needed to thrive in the modern world. That’s why – as part of our unique three-pillared approach – we’ll focus on your personal growth and help you develop essential future-focused skills.
Our ground-breaking Supercurricular programme is specifically designed to help you fulfil your long-term ambitions. Through six strands – which include programmes, awards, and competitions; clubs and societies; and further personal development – you’ll create a strong portfolio of experiences that will help you stand out from the crowd. Students who join us in Year 9 have even more time to identify and shape their route to success.
You’ll construct your pathway in consultation with your designated Strategy Tutor. If you want to become a lawyer, for example, you can develop your public speaking skills through a LAMDA course. We have links with local hospitals and medical schools, which offer real-world work experience. Want to deep-dive into a topic you’re passionate about? Then you can study for the Extended Project Qualification (EPQ), which is the equivalent to half an A-level.
At every stage of your learning journey, we’ll help you develop the characteristics, values, and transferable skills you’ll need to flourish here, at university, and beyond. On Nord Anglia’s award-winning Global Campus platform, for instance, you’ll collaborate, compete, and take on challenges with learners from around the world, whether it’s taking part in an international music showcase or virtually climbing Mount Kilimanjaro.
Wellbeing runs through the heart of everything we do at OIC Brighton. We know that happy, healthy students achieve more, which is why our rigorous academic approach is underpinned by an outstanding pastoral support system. Our Deputy Principal (Pastoral and Wellbeing), Head of Boarding, and Strategy Tutors promote a culture of self-care, respect, and equality. This creates an aspirational environment where like-minded students are supported to be ambitious and take on any challenge.
OIC Brighton is a place of ambition and aspiration; a closeknit community that provides the wellbeing support and level of challenge our young people need to thrive. Studying and living alongside like-minded students from around the world, you’ll feel inspired to exceed expectations and achieve great things.
OIC Brighton is a special place to live and learn. We’re a dynamic community where everybody works hard and loves a challenge. Our culture of excellence is driven by an exceptional team of teachers and staff, who set high expectations and are committed to helping you achieve your goals.
Of course, we also want you to be happy. That’s why we place health and wellbeing at the heart of college life. From weekly mental and physical health sessions and our OICB ROCKS ‘five ways to wellbeing’ programme, to one-to-one pastoral care from a dedicated Strategy Tutor, you’ll have all the support you need to flourish academically, emotionally, and socially.
Our beautiful campus enhances our sense of community, with our boarding houses and teaching buildings all on the same single site. You’ll join one of our four Houses, too, which cultivates a sense of belonging and inclusion, and provides opportunities for fun and competition across the age groups.
Home to students from more than 20 countries, we’re also a truly international college. You’ll study alongside some of the brightest young minds in the world, bonding over shared passions and goals, and creating unforgettable memories and connections that last a lifetime.
OIC Brighton is a proud member of the Nord Anglia Education family, too. This connects our students to unique global experiences and opportunities, including an immediate network of peers and alumni across the world.
OIC Brighton students are the pioneers of the future; the next generation of global change-makers, leaders, and thinkers. Our progressive ethos will inspire you to make a positive difference in our community – and develop the values, attributes, and understanding to go on and shape the world around us.
Being part of our vibrant international family enriches our students’ experience, broadening their horizons, creating a sense of purpose, and unlocking a breadth of opportunities.
As a community, we place great value on attributes like leadership, resilience, and teamwork. Each year, our students take part in the Young Enterprise Competition, which gives them an insight into the real-world challenges and opportunities of running a business. In the process, they gain hands-on experience, grow in confidence, and cultivate a strong sense of entrepreneurialism.
Our young people also proactively organise their own activities, including student-led clubs and societies through our Supercurricular programme. Founding their own groups, working with others, and following their passions demonstrates determination and commitment, and looks great on university applications.
While you’re with us, you’ll also learn about the challenges facing our planet – and take action to address them – through our exclusive collaboration with UNICEF. You’ll explore pressing issues, including climate change and the UN Sustainable Development Goals, through debates, challenges, and projects on our Global Campus platform. Our students also learn to collaborate, communicate with passion, and find creative solutions to some of the world’s toughest problems through Model United Nations activities and conferences.
We encourage our students to take part in The Duke of Edinburgh’s International Award, too. Through the Award, you’ll set their own goals and challenges, and commit to making a difference in our community. The Award builds confidence and self-esteem, and teaches essential skills for the future, including resourcefulness and the ability to solve problems.
Liz Free
Principal, Oxford International College Brighton
JOIN THE OIC BRIGHTON COMMUNITY
We’re delighted you’re considering Oxford International College Brighton for the next stage of your education. Your journey to success starts with our friendly admissions team, who will guide you through our application process.
Submit your application form.
We’ll then offer you a place.
Our News
FIND OUR INDEPENDENT SCHOOL IN BRIGHTON
At Oxford International College Brighton, you’ll follow your own pathway to success. Inspired to go above and beyond, you’ll achieve outstanding results that will take you to your dream university.
OIC Brighton Ovingdean Hall, Greenways, Ovingdean, Brighton East Sussex BN2 7BA

pageCache.pageTitle: Oxford International College Brighton Celebrates Outstanding GCSE Results
pageCache.text:
Visit OIC Brighton, Your Way
Oxford International College Brighton Celebrates Outstanding GCSE Results 2026
An outstanding 75% of all grades awarded at highest levels (grades 9-6)
Students at Oxford International College Brighton are celebrating an exceptional set of GCSE results, with 62% of all grades awarded at A*/A equivalent level and three quarters of grades awarded at the equivalent of A*-B. Overall, 95% of grades achieved a standard pass or above.
The results reflect the ambition, determination and hard work of students, supported by dedicated teachers and families who have worked alongside them throughout their educational journey.
Strength Across all Subjects
Success was evident across the curriculum, with particularly strong outcomes in Mathematics, the Sciences, English and Languages. Mathematics students achieved an outstanding 81% of grades at A*/A equivalent levels, whilst Chemistry students secured 71% of grades at A*/A equivalent levels and more than half achieved the highest grades available. English Language and English Literature both recorded a 100% pass rate, whilst students studying English as a Second Language achieved exceptional success, with 82% securing A*/A equivalent outcomes.
What is particularly encouraging is the breadth of achievement across the College. Students excelled across mathematics, sciences, English, languages, humanities and creative subjects, demonstrating both academic excellence and a willingness to embrace challenge.
These results also build on the College's strong academic performance in recent years. Compared with 2025, the proportion of top grades increased across all headline measures, with particularly strong growth in grades 9-8 and 9-7. The results reflect the College's continued focus on academic excellence, high expectations and personalised support for every student.
Results that show Ambition
Liz Free, Principal of Oxford International College Brighton, said:
“We are immensely proud of our students and all they have achieved. These results represent far more than examination outcomes. They are the culmination of years of commitment, resilience and hard work. Our students have embraced challenge, supported one another and demonstrated the ambition that sits at the heart of our College community.
What is particularly pleasing is the breadth of achievement. Students have excelled across mathematics, sciences, English, languages, humanities and creative subjects, achieving outstanding outcomes whilst pursuing ambitious goals and supporting one another throughout their educational journey.
Today is a celebration of everything our students have achieved. We congratulate every student on their success and thank our staff and families for the encouragement and support they have provided throughout this journey.”
Oxford International College Brighton remains committed to providing a challenging and supportive learning environment in which students are encouraged to think ambitiously, work hard and develop the knowledge, skills and character needed for future success.
Understanding the GCSE Grading System
To support comparison with previous grading systems, grades 9-7 are broadly equivalent to the former A/A grades*, whilst grades 9-6 are broadly equivalent to A-B grades*.

pageCache.pageTitle: Teaching Students to Think Like Problem-Solvers, Not Just Pass Exams | OIC Brighton
pageCache.text:
Visit OIC Brighton, Your Way
Teaching Students to Think Like Problem-Solvers, Not Just Pass Exams
One of the greatest challenges facing education today is preparing young people for a world where information is available in seconds. Questions can be answered instantly by search engines and AI.
The ability to think critically, evaluate evidence and solve unfamiliar problems is a skill that we as humans are in danger of losing. Education must go beyond passing exams. It should focus on developing thoughtful, analytical and resilient problem-solvers. “When Will I Ever Need This?” A common question heard in classrooms everywhere. The answer is not found in one specific fact or formula. Instead, it lies in how scientific thinking helps students understand the world around them and confidently question the information they encounter.
Bringing Science to Life
Curiosity at the Centre of Learning
These experiences are designed not only to engage, but to develop curiosity. From Year 9 onwards, students are encouraged to think beyond simply finding the right answer. Lessons are often built around questions such as:
“What happens when...?”
“What happens if...?”
Building Deeper Thinking
Thinking in an Age of AI
Navigating a World of Information
In an age of misinformation, clickbait headlines and conflicting online sources, the ability to think critically has never been more important. Through Physics, students learn how evidence is gathered, how conclusions are formed and how theories are tested. They are encouraged to follow a structured approach:
Observe the evidence
Interpret the findings
Evaluate the conclusions
Skills for Life, Not Just the Classroom
These steps reflect the work of scientists and engineers. More importantly, they mirror the skills needed to navigate everyday life. Whether assessing a claim on social media, interpreting statistics in the news or weighing up competing arguments, students must be able to distinguish evidence from opinion and conclusions from assumptions.
Preparing for the Future
Ultimately, our goal is not simply to produce students who can answer examination questions. It is to develop young people who are confident asking questions of their own, and who have the skills to find meaningful answers. Examinations may measure what students know at a single moment in time. Problem-solving, curiosity and critical thinking equip them for a lifetime.

pageCache.pageTitle: Starting Boarding School Near Brighton | A Practical Guide for Families
pageCache.text:
Visit OIC Brighton, Your Way
Starting Boarding School Near Brighton | A Practical Guide for Families
Not every exceptional boarding school is in the middle of a city. Some of the best are somewhere quieter, somewhere that gives students the space to focus, to think and to develop at their own pace. OIC Brighton sits in Ovingdean, a small village on the Sussex coast, four miles east of Brighton and right on the edge of Beacon Hill Local Nature Reserve.
Few schools can offer such a distinctive balance: a calm, focused environment with sea views, open countryside and one of the UK's most vibrant cities just twelve minutes away. For families exploring boarding schools near Brighton, it is worth considering how that combination benefits a student's day-to-day life.
A Campus Built for Focus
There is a reason some of the world's most respected schools are not in city centres. The environment in which students live and study has a direct effect on their ability to concentrate, to rest properly and to develop as individuals.
Ovingdean provides the ideal conditions for students to grow. Away from urban noise and distraction, students have the mental space to engage deeply with their studies, to build lasting friendships within the boarding community and to develop the habits of independent thinking that competitive universities look for.
Research published in the journal Environment and Behavior (2023) found that students in campus environments with access to natural settings report significantly higher levels of concentration and wellbeing than those in dense urban environments. The Sussex coast, in this sense, is not just a pleasant backdrop. It plays an important role in supporting students’ learning and quality of life.
Brighton on the Doorstep
Twelve minutes by car separates the college from Brighton city centre. Students have access to everything a world-class coastal city offers: culture, restaurants, independent shops, music, events and a thriving international community, without those things being a constant presence outside their window.
Brighton is there when students want it. The campus is there when they need to focus. That balance is seldom found at a boarding school, and it is one of the key factors that distinguishes OIC Brighton.
What the Transition Actually Involves
Starting at a boarding school is always a significant step. A new community, new academic expectations, a new rhythm to daily life. For students coming to OIC Brighton from abroad or from other parts of the UK, the Ovingdean setting can help make that transition feel more manageable.
For new students, the calmer surroundings are less overwhelming than a busy city-centre campus. The boarding community is self-contained enough that friendships form quickly. And Brighton, when students are ready to explore it, is there as a reward rather than a distraction.
A few things that help in those early weeks: • Engaging with the boarding house community from day one, rather than waiting to feel comfortable first • Making the most of the natural environment around the campus, including Beacon Hill Local Nature Reserve, as a way to decompress • Planning an early visit into Brighton so the city becomes familiar • Reaching out to the pastoral team early, not just when something goes wrong
A Community With Global Reach
OIC Brighton attracts students from across the world. The combination of a focused campus environment and the cultural accessibility of Brighton makes it particularly appealing to international families who want their child to experience authentic UK life without being overwhelmed by it.
The friendships formed in a smaller, residential community tend to be close ones. Students eat together, study together and spend weekends together. The shared experience of living in a distinctive place, on the Sussex coast with a city nearby, becomes part of what bonds them.
Before You Arrive: A Practical Checklist
• Travel to Ovingdean: The campus is in Ovingdean, East Sussex. Brighton city centre and Brighton train station are approximately twelve minutes by car. Gatwick Airport is around forty minutes away. Before travelling, international students should speak with the boarding team to ensure a smooth arrival and to enquire about airport collection services. • UK SIM card: Pick one up at the airport or order online before arrival. A working UK number from day one makes the first week considerably easier for both students and parents. • Bank account: International students will need a UK bank account for day-to-day spending. Some banks allow you to open an account before arriving in the UK. Ask the admissions team for guidance on which options work best for students. • GP registration: Register with a local GP as soon as possible after arrival. The boarding team can advise on the nearest practice. This is particularly important for students who take regular medication. • Medication and prescriptions: Bring a sufficient supply of any regular medication to cover the first term, along with documentation from your doctor. UK prescriptions work differently and establishing care with a new GP takes time. • Key contacts at the school: Save the admissions team, boarding house and pastoral lead numbers before you travel. Know who to call if anything goes wrong on arrival day. • Currency: Have some cash in pounds for the first few days. Card payments are widely accepted but cash is useful while you are finding your feet.
What to Pack: The Things Families Often Forget
Most families cover the essentials: bedding, clothing, school supplies. Here are the things that regularly get left behind: • Plug adaptor: Essential for international students. The UK uses a three-pin plug. Bring a universal adaptor or buy one at the airport. • A waterproof layer and walking shoes: The Sussex coast is beautiful but the weather along Marine Drive can be brisk and unpredictable. Packing a decent windproof and waterproof jacket is recommended. If your child plans to walk or run along the clifftop, proper footwear makes that much more enjoyable. • A small first aid kit: Paracetamol, plasters, antihistamine, cold and flu tablets. The boarding house will have supplies but having your own for minor ailments is convenient. • Something from home: A photograph, a familiar blanket, a small object with meaning. The first few nights in a new place are easier with something familiar nearby. • Reusable water bottle: The campus and surrounding area have good water access. A reusable bottle is practical for days out and walks along the coast. • Study supplies beyond the basics: Index cards, highlighters, sticky notes, a small personal whiteboard for your room. Students who set up their study space well in the first week tend to use it more consistently throughout term.[VK1.1]
Taking the Next Step
OIC Brighton offers A Level and GCSE programmes within one of the most distinctive settings in UK boarding education. If you are considering boarding school near Brighton for September entry, the best next step is a is to get in touch with our team.

pageCache.pageTitle: Why Psychology Is One of the Most Important Subjects for the Future | OIC Brighton
pageCache.text:
Visit OIC Brighton, Your Way
Why Psychology Is One of the Most Important Subjects for the Future
When people think about psychology, they often think about therapy, counselling, or mental health. While these are important areas, they represent only a small part of what psychology has become.
A Subject Like No Other
Psychology is one of the most versatile subjects a student can study because it occupies a unique position between the sciences and the humanities. It explores some of the most fundamental questions about human behaviour, thought and emotion, while applying the same scientific principles that underpin subjects such as biology and chemistry. Students are often surprised by the breadth of the discipline. Within a single course, they may study the biology of the brain, the influence of genetics, memory and cognition, mental health, social influence, child development, research methodology and statistical analysis. Few subjects offer such a diverse intellectual experience.
Learning to Think Critically
What makes psychology particularly valuable is its commitment to evidence. Students are constantly encouraged to question assumptions, evaluate competing explanations and examine the quality of the evidence that supports a claim. In an age where information is abundant and opinions are everywhere, the ability to distinguish between evidence and assertion has never been more important. The need for these skills is becoming increasingly apparent. We are living through a period of unprecedented technological and social change. Artificial intelligence is transforming industries, communication is instant and global, and information can be generated, shared and consumed at a scale unimaginable only a decade ago. Many of the careers our students will enter are likely to look very different by the time they graduate from university. This emphasis on critical thinking is increasingly important across all disciplines. As explored in our recent article, Teaching Students to Think Like Problem-Solvers, Not Just Pass Exams, developing the ability to analyse information, question assumptions and solve complex problems is becoming just as valuable as academic knowledge itself. In such an environment, factual knowledge alone is no longer enough. Students need to be able to evaluate evidence, think critically, identify bias, interpret data and make informed decisions in situations where there may not be an obvious answer. Psychology develops precisely these skills. Students learn not simply what to think, but how to think.
The Science Behind Human Behaviour
Psychology provides students with a rare opportunity to understand both the scientific process and human behaviour. They learn how experiments are designed, how data is collected and analysed, and how researchers draw conclusions from evidence. At the same time, they explore why people think, feel and behave as they do. This combination of scientific rigour and human understanding is what makes psychology such a distinctive subject.
Why Human Understanding Still Matters
As technology advances, understanding human behaviour may become even more valuable. While machines can process vast quantities of information, they cannot fully explain the complexities of human relationships, motivation, decision-making, prejudice, conformity, memory or mental health. Psychology helps students understand the human factors that continue to shape our families, workplaces, communities and societies. Perhaps most importantly, it teaches that human behaviour is rarely simple. Students are encouraged to appreciate different perspectives, challenge their own assumptions and approach complex problems with curiosity rather than certainty. These are qualities that remain valuable regardless of whether a student goes on to study medicine, law, business, economics, education, marketing, neuroscience or psychology itself.
Psychology Beyond the Classroom
At Oxford International College Brighton, we see psychology as much more than preparation for an examination. It is a subject that develops analytical thinkers, careful researchers and reflective individuals. Students leave with a stronger understanding of science, a deeper appreciation of human behaviour and a set of skills that are applicable across a remarkable range of careers. In a rapidly changing world, the most valuable subjects are not necessarily those that prepare students for a single profession. They are the subjects that develop adaptable thinkers who can navigate uncertainty, evaluate new information and understand the people around them. Psychology achieves all three. It equips students with scientific literacy, critical thinking skills and a deeper understanding of human behaviour, qualities that will remain relevant long after specific technologies, industries and job titles have changed.
Looking Ahead
The future is difficult to predict. Human behaviour, however, will always matter. That is why psychology remains one of the most relevant and valuable subjects students can study.

Visit OIC Brighton, Your Way
PARENT ESSENTIALS
Welcome to the Oxford International College (OIC) Brighton family. On this page, you’ll find lots of useful information and links, covering everything from daily life on our amazing campus to important dates for your diary.
OUR CALENDAR: 2026-27
Keep track of key term, holiday, and event dates at OIC Brighton with our 2026-27 calendar.
EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO THRIVE
Every student’s journey to success extends beyond academics. Our pioneering approach will nurture your personal growth and career aspirations, ensuring you develop a breadth of essential future-focused skills.
Our ground-breaking Super curricular programme will help you fulfil your long-term ambitions. Through six strands – which include further personal development and applying to university – you’ll create a strong portfolio of relevant experiences, qualifications, and awards that will help you stand out from the crowd.
Our student-led programme of clubs and societies nurtures individual talents, giving our young people the opportunity to bond over shared interests. Whatever your passion – whether it’s science, sports, the arts, or something a little bit different – we’ll help you to plan and run your own activities.
Throughout your learning journey, we’ll help you develop the ‘growth mindset’, characteristics, and values you’ll need to flourish here, at university, and beyond. Challenges on our award-winning Global Campus platform nurture critical thinking, creativity, and digital literacy skills, while our comprehensive wellbeing approach builds resilience, confidence, and adaptability.
Exclusive collaborations with UNICEF and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) make our school a truly unique place to learn. In our state-of-the-art labs, you’ll use ‘design thinking’ to solve STEAM challenges set by MIT professors. You’ll also explore pressing global issues, including climate change and the UN Sustainable Development Goals, through UNICEF-curated projects.
LIVING IN BRIGHTON
Brighton is an incredibly vibrant city that’s easy to navigate on foot or by bike – and our campus is just minutes from the heart of the action. There’s so much to see and do, from exploring independent shops and cafés in The Lanes to enjoying a quintessentially English seaside experience at the world-famous pavilion and pier. Brighton beach is great place to enjoy a picnic with friends or go for a scenic stroll, too. Looking for something a bit more energetic? You can paddleboard or kayak off the coast, or head to the South Downs for a hike or bike ride.
ALL THE INFORMATION YOU NEED
We know how important it is to provide the detailed information you need to settle in quickly – and make the most of your time with us. From academic policies and expectations to safeguarding and student services, our comprehensive handbook contains everything there is to know about life at our college.

FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQS)
Do your students wear a uniform?
In Years 9, 10, and 11, our students wear a casual uniform comprising polo shirts, chinos or a skirt, a zip-up sweatshirt, and plain shoes or trainers. This ensures everyone looks smart and tidy, feels comfortable, and is ready to tackle anything the day throws at them. Our Year 12 and 13 students can either wear their own clothes during the college day or items of uniform. For sports, students wear our bespoke college kit.
What meals will I eat?
Our boarders enjoy a freshly prepared breakfast, lunch, and dinner every day, which they eat together in the college’s communal dining room. Our menu has been carefully crafted with wellbeing and physical health in mind, taking inspiration from different cuisines, and giving students a real home from home experience. This includes a creative lunch menu, which includes two main choices, as well as a street food-style option, sides, and dessert.
How do you support student wellbeing?
Student health, happiness, and wellbeing is our priority. We know how important it is to help our young people settle into college life, both socially and academically. That’s why the education we offer is underpinned by an outstanding pastoral system, which nurtures personal growth and provides the 24/7 care our students need to thrive.
Throughout your time here, you’ll be supported by a team of experts, including your Strategy Tutor, our Boarding House Team, and Counsellor. Our OICB ROCKS ‘five ways to wellbeing’ programme promotes positive emotional and physical health, too. You can also access bespoke support in our dedicated wellbeing centre.
Is the college open to students of all nationalities?
Yes! We’re proud to be a truly international school that’s home to students from more than 20 countries. Living and learning here, you’ll study alongside some of the brightest young minds in the world, bonding over shared passions and goals, and creating memories and connections that last a lifetime.
THE LATEST NEWS AND EVENTS
Passionate about their subjects – and committed to your goals – our trailblazing teachers cultivate an ambitious yet supportive culture where everybody thrives.

pageCache.pageTitle: What to Expect in Your First Term at OIC Brighton
pageCache.text:
Visit OIC Brighton, Your Way
What to Expect in Your First Term at OIC Brighton
The first term at a boarding school is one of the most formative periods in a young person's education. New people, new routines, new expectations. And at OIC Brighton, a new landscape: the Sussex coast, open countryside and a city just twelve minutes away.
Here is what the first term at OIC Brighton typically looks like, and what helps students make the most of it.
Arriving in Ovingdean
Arrival day is carefully structured. Induction sessions, introductions to the boarding house, time to settle in and find your bearings. The Ovingdean campus has a self-contained quality that helps students orient themselves quickly. Many students comment on the setting itself in those first days: the sea visible from the campus, the open sky, the quiet that is so different from what they expected. For most, within a week or two, it becomes something they cherish.
The First Few Weeks
The early weeks are about building foundations: understanding the academic expectations, getting to know housemates, establishing a study rhythm. A few things that consistently help students settle well:
• Staying engaged with the boarding house community in the evenings rather than isolating in their room • Getting outside and using the natural environment around the campus, even briefly, between study sessions • Planning an early group trip into Brighton so the city feels accessible rather than distant • Being honest with tutors and house staff about how the adjustment is going The pastoral team at OIC Brighton is experienced in supporting students through this transition, while the close-knit nature of the community ensures that every student feels seen.
Academic Life
A Level study demands a level of independent engagement that can feel unfamiliar at first. The structured environment of a boarding campus helps: study periods are built into the day, and the relative quiet of Ovingdean removes many of the distractions that city-centre students face. By mid-term, most students have found a rhythm. Teachers are approachable, and small class sizes allow them to build strong, individual relationships with each student.
Brighton as a Weekend Option
During the week, the campus and its surroundings provide everything students need. At weekends, Brighton opens up. Students head into the city for food, culture, shopping and a change of scene. The twelve-minute journey is short enough to feel easy, and long enough that the return to campus feels like coming back to somewhere calm.
Many students find this rhythm, focused week with the city at the weekend, one of the things they appreciate most about the OIC Brighton experience.
By the End of Term
Most students leave their first term at OIC Brighton with a clearer sense of who they are. The combination of academic challenge, a close community and a supportive setting tends to accelerate the kind of personal development that boarding school is, at its best, designed to produce.
The Sussex coast has a way of putting things in perspective. Students who arrive anxious about the transition often find, by Christmas, that Ovingdean has become somewhere that truly feels like home.

Visit OIC Brighton, Your Way
HOW WE TEACH
OIC Brighton teachers strive for excellence in everything they do, using their specialist knowledge, abundant experience, and pioneering spirit to bring out the best in every student.
LEARNING FROM THE BEST
OIC Brighton is home to the very best UK and international teachers. Meticulously chosen, they bring a wealth of qualifications and global experience to our classrooms.
Our exceptional educators are pioneers in their subject field or specialism. Many have also excelled in the industry they now teach in. Every day, their breadth of knowledge and expertise – alongside their unrivalled enthusiasm for their discipline – bring learning to life in new and exhilarating ways.
Crucially, our dedicated team are committed to building a strong partnership with you. Guided by your Strategy Tutor, they’ll provide the constant support and mentoring you need to excel academically and flourish as a person.
MEET OUR LEADERSHIP TEAM
Our senior leadership team sets high expectations, creating a culture that inspires excellence. Their commitment to happiness and wellbeing complements this ambitious approach, ensuring our students have everything they need to thrive.
Liz Free is an internationally recognised school leader with experience across UK and global education. She joins with a strong record in driving growth, building inclusive communities and placing students, staff and families at the heart of school life. Her career includes leading the International School Rheintal in Switzerland as CEO and Director, alongside senior roles at the British School in the Netherlands and Oxford University Press. She has also served as a Global Board Member for Tes and Trustee of WomenEd, with her leadership recognised by the IFIP Global Inclusion Award and a TES International Headteacher of the Year shortlist.
Previously Deputy Head (Pastoral) and Designated Safeguarding Lead at a leading UK preparatory school, Jonno is committed to developing innovative approaches that enhance student wellbeing. In previous roles, he has successfully implemented a variety of pioneering projects, from creating a school-wide ‘culture of kindness’ to a ‘caught being kind’ initiative. Jonno’s dedication to welfare, safeguarding, and pastoral care ensures our students thrive.
Tom Leighton FTIOB is Director of Boarding at Oxford International College Brighton, bringing over 15 years of experience in leading vibrant and supportive boarding communities. He holds advanced safeguarding qualifications, including Level 5 Safeguarding Children’s Manager training and the Advanced Certificate for Designated Safeguarding Leads. Fluent in English, French, and Spanish, Tom is committed to creating inclusive, nurturing environments where students can thrive. Tom also is our UKVI Authorising Officer.
Results-driven operations leader with extensive experience in academic management, data analysis, timetabling, and project leadership. Adept at optimising institutional processes, managing teams, and leading data-driven decision-making to enhance student performance and operational efficiency. Proven track record in implementing educational technologies, overseeing student onboarding, and contributing to senior leadership initiatives. Passionate about fostering an inclusive and high-achieving learning environment.
Jo is an experienced Admissions professional passionate about delivering an exceptional family journey from enquiry to acceptance and beyond. With strong interpersonal and cross‑cultural communication skills, she builds positive relationships with families and agents from diverse backgrounds. Since 2014, she has worked in a fast‑paced independent school Admissions team, consistently exceeding targets. Creative and solutions‑focused, she approaches challenges with a growth mindset and a “can‑do” attitude, inspiring others with her positive approach to work and life.
HELPING OUR TEACHERS GROW
At our college, we aspire to excellence in everything we do. We love a challenge, we work hard, and we’re always looking to improve. This ethos is driven by our ambitious international team. Through shared observations, departmental discussions, and subject-specific training, OIC Brighton staff continually reflect on and refine what we do. Their breadth of global experience unlocks new ideas and approaches, too.
We make sure our teachers have the support they need to achieve their goals. This includes access to a wealth of courses and development opportunities on the award-winning Nord Anglia University training platform.
SETTING THE BAR HIGH
To guarantee the highest standards, we actively recruit the world’s best UK and international teachers and pastoral staff.
Every single one of our educators is handpicked, based not only on their outstanding qualifications, subject knowledge, and real-world experience, but also their commitment to our ambitious ethos. As soon as they join us, our staff go through an extensive induction programme that immerses them in our culture and values.
Being part of the Nord Anglia Education global family ensures we lead the way in the sector. Their Global Education Team drives success in academics, quality assurance, accreditation, and safeguarding.
JOIN OUR TALENTED TEAM
OIC Brighton is a truly unique global college. Having opened in 2023, it’s a place where you can make your mark, shaping our culture of excellence and nurturing the next generation of pioneers and original thinkers. You’ll love working on our beautiful countryside campus, too, which is just minutes away from the coast and city.
OIC Brighton is home to gifted students from around the world – and you can join them. Start your journey to our pioneering college by filling in our online enquiry form today.

pageCache.text:
Visit OIC Brighton, Your Way
GUARDIANSHIP REQUIREMENTS
To ensure every student is fully supported while living away from home, a UK-based guardian or close relative is required where parents do not provide day-to-day care during term time. This typically applies where parents live overseas, live more than 2 hours from the school, or are away for extended periods. These arrangements apply to all students, regardless of age, nationality, or visa status, and form an important part of our commitment to student wellbeing and safeguarding.
CHOOSING AN ACCREDITED GUARDIAN FOR STUDENT SUPPORT
Where possible, we strongly recommend that families appoint a fully accredited guardianship agency. This means an agency accredited by AEGIS (the Association for the Education and Guardianship of International Students) or fully accredited by the Boarding Schools’ Association (BSA), ensuring they meet recognised standards for safeguarding, student care, and service quality (please note that BSA provisional accreditation is not accepted). Accredited providers offer trained staff, established and vetted host family networks, and reliable support in both day-to-day matters and unexpected situations.
The College works closely with a trusted panel of four fully accredited agencies Belgravia Guardians, Bright World Guardianships, Crown International, and UKGuardianship who provide responsive, high-quality support tailored to each family’s needs. These agencies work in partnership with the College and parents to ensure continuity, regular communication, and structured support, promoting each student’s stability, wellbeing, and overall experience. We encourage families to select a guardian from this panel wherever possible.
WHAT IS A NOMINATED GUARDIAN OR CLOSE RELATIVE?
A close relative living in the UK;
A family friend living in the UK;
A non-accredited guardianship agency.
GUARDIAN APPROVAL AND VETTING REQUIREMENTS
Every student’s application journey is different, so we’d encourage you to get in touch with our team to find out how it’ll work for you.
